The core operators define a hierarchical framework for evaluating fantasy players through rank estimation (pwe), optimizing rosters dynamically (dwe), and aggregating positional contributions (xwe). These primitives form a closed-loop system where pwe provides input scores, dwe selects optimal lineups based on those scores, and xwe computes cumulative team performance. The failure mode occurs when lookup functions like ome or dF return invalid data, leading to incorrect rankings or incomplete selections. Dualities emerge between static rank estimation and dynamic optimization—static ranks provide priors while dynamic optimization refines them. In GSI, these operators support Bayesian inference pipelines that update belief states about player value over time. In GSE, they enable real-time decision-making under uncertainty by simulating various lineup configurations and computing expected utilities.
